hypothesis: Using only issuer-disclosed Broadcom FY2026 facts and the full accounting-feasible range for the undisclosed Q4 segment mix, FY2027 company revenue growth of 18.83753816% can still be achieved with AI semiconductor growth below 30% across every feasible Q4 mix, if Q1-Q3 observed growth rates for non-AI semiconductor and infrastructure software are carried forward for one year.

decision_rule.USE: Use as a robust near-term growth anchor only if required FY2027 AI semiconductor growth remains below 30% across the full Q4 feasible segment interval and the result does not depend materially on extrapolating Q1-Q3 non-AI bucket growth.
decision_rule.CONDITION: Retain as a near-term sensitivity anchor if required AI growth is below 30% across the full Q4 accounting interval, but one-year extrapolation of Q1-Q3 non-AI bucket growth remains an assumption.
decision_rule.REJECT: Reject if any accounting-feasible Q4 mix requires AI semiconductor growth of 30% or more, or if the conclusion requires a fabricated point estimate for Q4 segment mix.
decision_rule.UNVERIFIED: Use if issuer-reported total revenue, AI revenue, or the prior canonical three-bucket growth facts cannot be identified.

method.q4_accounting_identity: Q4 non-AI semiconductor + Q4 infrastructure software = 34.8 - 21.7 = 13.1 billion USD.

q4_interval.interpretation: This is the broadest non-negative accounting-feasible interval. No unpublished segment mix is inferred.

fy2027_non_ai_assumptions.source: Observed Q1-Q3 FY2026 versus Q1-Q3 FY2025 growth from the prior canonical three-bucket artifact.
fy2027_non_ai_assumptions.scope: One-year sensitivity assumption only; not issuer guidance and not a multi-year forecast.

method.required_ai_growth_formula: required AI growth = (FY2027 target revenue - FY2027 non-AI semiconductor - FY2027 infrastructure software) / FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue - 1
method.missing_data_policy: Do not choose a point estimate for Q4 software or non-AI semiconductor revenue. Evaluate both endpoints of the full feasible interval; the required AI growth is linear in the Q4 mix, so endpoint evaluation bounds the entire interval.

endpoint_cases.case: all Q4 residual assigned to non-AI semiconductor
all Q4 residual assigned to infrastructure software

benchmark_comparison.interpretation: Separating non-AI semiconductor from infrastructure software widens the required AI growth range materially, especially on the upper side, but the entire accounting-feasible interval remains below 30%.

capital_allocation_implication: Broadcom's 18.83753816% FY2027 company-growth comparator survives the Q4 segment-mix uncertainty under a one-year continuation of observed non-AI bucket growth: AI semiconductor growth of roughly 25.7% to 28.0% is sufficient across the full non-negative Q4 accounting interval. This supports retaining 18.83753816% only as a near-term CONDITION sensitivity anchor. It does not justify a multi-year AVGO growth assumption or a portfolio-weight change.

risk_and_validation.time_series_risk_metrics: not applicable; this is a forward fundamental boundary study, not a return backtest
risk_and_validation.model_risk: The result depends on carrying Q1-Q3 observed non-AI semiconductor and infrastructure software growth forward for one year.
risk_and_validation.data_risk: Q4 segment mix remains undisclosed; this artifact avoids a fabricated point estimate by bounding the entire accounting-feasible interval.
risk_and_validation.comparison_to_current_q4_ai_guidance: Current Q4 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue guidance is +236% year over year, far above the 25.7% to 28.0% FY2027 growth required by this sensitivity, but current growth is not assumed to persist.

limitations: Broadcom has not disclosed Q4 FY2026 semiconductor-solutions and infrastructure-software guidance separately.
The full accounting interval includes economically extreme Q4 mixes; it is intentionally broad to avoid hidden assumptions.
Q1-Q3 non-AI bucket growth rates are observed historical growth, not FY2027 issuer guidance.
The result supports only a one-year sensitivity anchor; it does not validate FY2028-FY2030 company growth.
OpenAI and other multi-year AI deployment evidence is not converted into revenue without an issuer-disclosed revenue-recognition schedule.
next_hypothesis: Can Broadcom's FY2027-FY2030 AI semiconductor growth be bounded from issuer-disclosed deployment capacity and customer commitments without converting gigawatts directly into revenue, so the NVDA/AVGO two-sided five-year growth boundary can use year-specific intervals instead of flat growth anchors?
